Here’s a summary of the provided article excerpt:

New data reveals that public bodies spent a record £3.4 billion on private consultants last year, marking a 62% increase since 2019-20. Despite hopes that spending would return to pre-pandemic levels, the surge in consultant fees has persisted. The figures highlight the difficulty facing the new government, which aims to cut such spending by half. Recent contracts, including a £223 million deal with KPMG to train civil servants, have already been awarded, totaling nearly £650 million since the election. Critics argue that excessive reliance on consultants is wasteful, as they often lack deep organizational understanding to provide meaningful solutions.
